correctness.rationale: For each fixed 20-vertex graph, the decision predicate accepts exactly those subsets whose unselected vertices have pairwise distinct nonempty open-neighborhood intersections with the subset. The C++ program loops over all 1,048,576 masks with a 2-subset-disjointness Desargues model and the generalized Petersen dodecahedral model. The Python program independently loops over all combinations using GP(10,3) and GP(10,2), checks an explicit Desargues graph isomorphism, and reproduces all 21 coefficients. Both executed successfully. Subtracting the two vectors leaves positive differences at exactly cardinalities 7 through 13; summing the corresponding positive Bernoulli monomials proves strict reliability dominance for every \(0<p<1\), with endpoint equality. The conclusion is only for the two graphs.

originality.rationale: The closest 2014–2015 primary literature establishes ordinary locating domination and upper bounds for cubic or girth-five graphs, not these complete 21-coefficient enumerators. The two closest accessible public mathematical results enumerate minimum Desargues and dodecahedral code families but not the complete nonminimum spectra; their reported minimum counts agree with this result. Both full previous statements, the relevant primary-paper theorem sections and conclusions, and actual mathematical-result searches for exact coefficients, aliases, and reliability were compared by implication. No covering full polynomial or all-probability inequality was identified; unindexed priority remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed published or historical computer enumerations could have determined the same 21 coefficients under alternate locating/test-cover terminology.
The result is computationally exhaustive for two fixed graphs and has no independent scholarly validation; the source code and exact predicates are supplied to make such checks possible.
Only inspected source sections support comparisons with the two arXiv papers; no assertion that every historically relevant paper was retrieved.

value.rationale: The location-domination polynomial is the exact natural enumerator for deployments of local monitors that must both cover and distinguish every unmonitored location. Known minima alone do not determine success probabilities at intermediate deployment densities. These two canonical cubic order-20 networks have strictly ordered success counts for every budget 7 through 13, equal counts beyond the sharp cutoff, and consequently strict reliability dominance over the whole open probability interval. The complete finite invariant and the uniform stochastic comparison have direct mathematical significance even without an infinite-family theorem.
